concepts.def: A gas in the atmosphere that absorbs long wavelength radiation emitted by the Earth's surface and re-radiates some of it back towards the Earth. Water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases.
The specification names water vapour, carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4). Nitrogen and oxygen, which together make up about 99% of the air, are not greenhouse gases.
The process by which greenhouse gases in the atmosphere maintain temperatures on Earth high enough to support life. Without it the Earth's surface would be far colder.
Radiation from the Sun. Most of it passes through the atmosphere without being absorbed by greenhouse gases and is absorbed by the Earth's surface, warming it.
Radiation emitted by the warmed Earth's surface. Its wavelength is longer than that of the radiation arriving from the Sun, and greenhouse gases absorb it.
Greenhouse gases absorb long wavelength radiation from the Earth and re-radiate it in all directions, including back towards the surface, so the surface stays warmer.
Burning fossil fuels (in power stations, vehicles and homes) and deforestation, which leaves fewer trees to remove carbon dioxide by photosynthesis.
Cattle and other livestock farming, and the decay of organic waste in landfill sites. Growing rice in flooded paddy fields also releases methane.
Checking of a scientist's methods, data and conclusions by other scientists working in the same field before the work is published.
The evidence for climate change does not fix a single exact outcome: measurements have limits, the climate system is complex and future emissions are unknown, so predictions are given as ranges.
A report presents only part of the evidence, or presents opinion or speculation as if it were established evidence, often to support a particular point of view.
A long-term change in the Earth's climate, caused mainly by an increase in the average global temperature of the atmosphere at the surface.
Sea level rise and flooding of low-lying land, more frequent and severe storms, changes to the amount and distribution of rainfall, and changes to the range of many wild species.
Risk combines how likely an effect is with how severe it would be. Climate change is global in scale, so the effects and the risks are not confined to the countries that emit the most.
The total amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases emitted over the full life cycle of a product, service or event.
Every stage from obtaining raw materials, through manufacture, transport and use, to disposal at the end of the product's useful life.
Using renewable energy or nuclear power, increasing energy efficiency, carbon capture and storage, carbon taxes and licences, and capturing methane from landfill and livestock.
Cost, the slow pace of scientific and technological development, disagreement between governments, lack of public information and education, and reluctance to change lifestyles.

concepts.term: communicating results to a wide range of audiences
concepts.def: Reporting findings beyond scientific journals, to the public, governments and industry, because those audiences take the decisions that the evidence affects and cannot act on evidence they never see.

mcqs.q: Which statement about greenhouse gases in the Earth's atmosphere is correct?
options: Water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane are all greenhouse gases.
Water vapour is a natural gas and so is not a greenhouse gas.
Only gases released by human activity act as greenhouse gases.
Greenhouse gases make up most of the atmosphere by volume.
mcqs.explain: These are the three greenhouse gases the specification names.

mcqs.q: What do greenhouse gases in the atmosphere do for living things on Earth?
options: They block the ultraviolet radiation coming from the Sun.
They pollute the air and are harmful to all living things.
They cool the Earth by reflecting sunlight into space.
They keep temperatures on Earth high enough to support life.
mcqs.explain: This is exactly what the specification says greenhouse gases maintain.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the greenhouse effect?
options: Long wavelength radiation passes through and short wavelength is absorbed.
Greenhouse gases reflect the incoming radiation back down to the ground.
Short wavelength radiation passes through; long wavelength is absorbed.
Greenhouse gases hold warm air near the ground, like a blanket.
mcqs.explain: Solar radiation passes through the atmosphere, and the long wavelength radiation emitted by the surface is absorbed by greenhouse gases.

mcqs.q: Radiation from the Sun passes through the atmosphere and is absorbed by the ground. What happens next?
options: The ground reflects the radiation back at the same wavelength.
The warmed surface emits longer wavelength radiation.
The surface emits radiation of an even shorter wavelength.
The warm air rises and is trapped by greenhouse gases.
mcqs.explain: The Earth's surface, being much cooler than the Sun, radiates at longer wavelengths.

mcqs.q: What do greenhouse gases do with the long wavelength radiation they absorb?
options: They re-radiate it in all directions, including back towards the Earth.
They reflect all of it straight back down to the Earth's surface.
They store it permanently, so the energy never leaves the gas.
They convert it into short wavelength radiation from the Sun.
mcqs.explain: Absorption is followed by re-radiation, and the part sent downwards keeps the surface warm.

mcqs.q: Which human activity increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
options: Growing rice in fields that are kept flooded all year.
Keeping large herds of cattle on grassland.
Burying more household waste in landfill sites.
Burning fossil fuels in power stations and vehicles.
mcqs.explain: Combustion of fossil fuels is a named human source of carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: Explain why cutting down large areas of forest increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the air.
options: Trees give out carbon dioxide, so cutting them down helps the air.
Cutting the trees down releases the methane that is stored in wood.
Fewer trees are left to remove carbon dioxide by photosynthesis.
Losing trees thins the ozone layer and lets more heat in.
mcqs.explain: Photosynthesis is the process that takes carbon dioxide out of the air, so removing trees reduces it.

mcqs.q: Which pair of human activities both increase the amount of methane in the atmosphere?
options: Landfill sites and burning of coal.
Cattle farming and rice growing.
Deforestation and cattle farming.
Aerosol sprays and air conditioning.
mcqs.explain: Livestock and flooded rice fields are both named methane sources.

mcqs.q: A student is asked to name two human activities that increase the amount of carbon dioxide. Which pair is correct?
options: Burning fossil fuels for electricity, and deforestation.
Cattle farming, and decay of waste in landfill sites.
Burning fossil fuels, and keeping herds of cattle.
Deforestation, and the melting of the polar ice.
mcqs.explain: These are the two carbon dioxide activities named in the specification.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes what scientists say about human activity and the Earth's temperature?
options: Scientists have now proved that human activity is the only possible cause of warming.
Scientists disagree with each other, so there is no reliable evidence at all.
The claim comes from opinions in the media rather than from measured data.
Based on peer-reviewed evidence, many scientists expect the Earth's surface to warm.
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's own statement of the scientific position.

mcqs.q: Why do different climate models give different predictions for future temperatures?
options: Climate models are built on opinion rather than on any real measured data.
The temperature of the whole of the atmosphere cannot be measured well.
Global climate is a very complex system, so models must be simplified.
The results of the models have not been checked by peer review.
mcqs.explain: The specification says such complex systems are difficult to model, which leads to simplified models.

mcqs.q: A newspaper article about climate change is described as biased. What does this mean?
options: Its thermometers were badly calibrated.
It presents only part of the evidence.
It disagrees with peer-reviewed research.
Its writer is uncertain about the outcome.
mcqs.explain: Bias here is selective use of evidence, or opinion presented as evidence.

mcqs.q: A website claims that the world is cooling, using two years of readings from one weather station. What is the best evaluation of this evidence?
options: The sample is too small and the period too short to show a global trend.
The evidence is strong because real temperatures were measured.
The evidence is worthless because a website is not a journal.
Two years is enough if the thermometer was accurate enough.
mcqs.explain: A global, long-term claim needs data from many places over many years.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a genuine uncertainty in the evidence base for global climate change?
options: Nobody had measured the temperature of the Earth before the year 2000.
Scientists made mistakes when they recorded their measurements.
It is not known whether carbon dioxide absorbs radiation.
Future emissions are not known, so predictions are given as a range.
mcqs.explain: What humans will emit in future is a real unknown, so models give ranges.

mcqs.q: Why is peer review of climate research important?
options: It proves that the conclusions are right and settles the matter for good.
It lets the general public vote on which scientific results to believe.
Other scientists check the methods and conclusions before publication.
It checks that the thermometers were properly calibrated.
mcqs.explain: Peer review is checking by other scientists in the same field.

mcqs.q: Why is a rise of about one degree in the average global temperature important?
options: Every place on Earth is now one degree warmer.
It shifts the climate of the whole Earth.
It is too small to change the weather at all.
It shows that the ozone layer is thinning.
mcqs.explain: An average across the whole planet moving is a large change to the climate system.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a potential effect of global climate change?
options: Sea level rise, causing flooding of low-lying land.
More acid rain falling on lakes and forests.
A larger hole in the ozone layer each spring.
An increase in deforestation and cattle farming.
mcqs.explain: Rising sea level and flooding are named potential effects.

mcqs.q: Which list contains only potential effects of global climate change?
options: Flooding, deforestation, more frequent storms and stronger winds.
Rising sea level, acid rain, changes to rainfall patterns.
Extreme weather, cattle farming, loss of some habitats.
Flooding, more extreme weather, changes to species distribution.
mcqs.explain: All three are potential effects the specification expects students to describe.

mcqs.q: A report says that the risk to a coastal city from climate change is high. What does describing the risk involve?
options: How severe the flooding would be, however unlikely it is.
How many people believe that the report is correct.
How likely the flooding is, and how severe it would be.
How likely the flooding is, however small the damage.
mcqs.explain: Risk combines the chance of an event with the size of its consequences.

mcqs.q: What is the carbon footprint of a product?
options: Carbon dioxide given off while the product is made.
Greenhouse gases emitted over its full life cycle.
The mass of carbon that the finished object contains.
The carbon dioxide released while the product is used.
mcqs.explain: The definition covers carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases across the whole life cycle.

mcqs.q: Which statement about a carbon footprint is correct?
options: It includes methane as well as carbon dioxide, at every stage.
It counts carbon dioxide only, from the factory stage.
It is the carbon locked inside the finished product.
It counts only the gases given off during its transport.
mcqs.explain: The definition covers carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, over the full life cycle.

mcqs.q: A company wants to reduce the carbon footprint of its factory. Which action would do this?
options: Fit filters to the chimneys to trap all the carbon dioxide.
Cut emissions only during manufacture.
Make the product from materials containing less carbon.
Take the factory's electricity from wind and solar farms.
mcqs.explain: Renewable electricity replaces fossil fuel combustion, so less carbon dioxide is emitted.

mcqs.q: Which action would reduce emissions of methane?
options: Bury much more waste in landfill so that the gas cannot escape.
Fit filters to the power station chimneys to trap the methane.
Collect the gas from landfill sites and burn it as a fuel.
Burn less coal in the power stations that are nearby.
mcqs.explain: Capturing the gas stops methane escaping into the atmosphere, and it is put to use as a fuel.

mcqs.q: Give one reason why actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions may be limited.
options: There is no evidence for the warming.
Alternative technologies cost a lot.
Emissions cannot be measured at all today.
The evidence has not yet been peer reviewed.
mcqs.explain: Cost is a named reason why action is limited.

mcqs.q: Climate scientists report their findings to the public, governments and industry, not only in scientific journals. Why does this matter?
options: The public can then vote on which findings are true.
It persuades the public to agree with the scientists.
Those groups make decisions that depend on the findings.
Reporting widely proves that the findings are correct.
mcqs.explain: Voters, governments and industry cannot act on evidence they never see, so results must reach them as well as other scientists.
